record.original_question: Does the degree-4 Sum-of-Squares relaxation for the clique number of the Paley graph beat the classical √p barrier by a polynomial factor? More precisely, does there exist ε > 0 such that the degree-4 SoS bound is O(p^{1/2−ε})?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 28. There exists ε > 0 such that the Sum-of-Squares relaxation of degree 4 for the clique number of the Paley graph gives a bound of O(p^{1/2−ε}).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p be an odd prime with p ≡ 1 (mod 4). The Paley graph G_p has vertex set F_p (the finite field of order p), with two distinct vertices u, v adjacent if and only if u − v is a nonzero quadratic residue in F_p. Let ω(G_p) denote the clique number of G_p.

For a graph G on vertex set V = {1,…,n}, the degree-4 Sum-of-Squares (SoS) relaxation of the clique number is the optimal value of the following pseudo-expectation problem: maximize Ẽ[∑_{i∈V} x_i] over linear functionals Ẽ on the space of polynomials in x_1,…,x_n of degree ≤ 4 satisfying
 (i) Ẽ[1] = 1;
 (ii) Ẽ[x_i^2 − x_i] = 0 for every i ∈ V (Boolean constraints);
 (iii) Ẽ[x_i x_j · q(x)] = 0 for every edge {i,j} ∉ E(G) (i.e., every non-edge) and every polynomial q with deg(x_i x_j q) ≤ 4 (independent-set constraint);
 (iv) Ẽ[p(x)^2] ≥ 0 for every polynomial p with deg(p) ≤ 2.
Denote this optimum by SoS_4(G).

It is classical (via the Hoffman/Lovász-type spectral bound) that SoS_4(G_p) = O(√p), and a lower bound SoS_4(G_p) = Ω(p^{1/3}) is known.

Question: Does there exist a constant ε > 0 such that
 SoS_4(G_p) = O(p^{1/2 − ε})
as p ranges over primes with p ≡ 1 (mod 4)?
artifact.category_tag: Sum-of-Squares relaxations / Paley graph clique number
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be open. Kunisky and Yu (2022/2023) established a lower bound of Ω(p^{1/3}) on the degree-4 SoS relaxation for the Paley graph clique number, and reported numerical experiments suggesting the value may scale as O(p^{1/2−ε}). However, no proof of such a polynomial improvement over the √p spectral barrier is known, and the conjecture remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A degree 4 sum-of-squares lower bound for the clique number of the Paley graph
status_evidence.snippet: The degree 4 SoS relaxation of the clique number of the Paley graph on p vertices has value at least Ω(p^{1/3}). Numerical experiments indicate that the value of the degree 4 SOS relaxation of the Paley graph may scale as O(p^{1/2 - ε}) for some ε > 0.
status_evidence.claim: A lower bound Ω(p^{1/3}) is proved; the upper bound O(p^{1/2−ε}) is supported only by numerical evidence and is conjectural.

status_evidence.title: On the clique number of the Paley Graph (problems 25-29) | Randomstrasse 101
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 28: there exists ε>0 such that the degree-4 SoS relaxation gives a bound O(p^{1/2−ε}).
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open conjecture on the Randomstrasse 101 problem page.
